items.title: 1.3 Salient features of the kingdoms of domain Eukarya

source_refs.note: Topic 1.3, printed pages 7-10, including the table of distinguishing characteristics of the kingdoms of the three domains and the opening of kingdom Animalia.

blocks.text: Domain Eukarya consists of the kingdoms Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. It includes all eukaryotes: organisms made of complex eukaryotic cells that contain a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. This topic looks at what sets each kingdom apart.

Kingdom Protista includes eukaryotes that are unicellular, colonial, filamentous or simply multicellular. Simple multicellular means that they do not have multicellular sex organs. There are three types of protists.

items: Protozoa are animal-like protists. They are unicellular and heterotrophic. Examples: Paramecium, Amoeba, Plasmodium and Trypanosoma.
Algae are plant-like protists. They have cell walls made of cellulose, contain chlorophyll and are autotrophs. Examples: Euglena and diatoms.
Myxomycota and Oomycota are fungi-like protists. They have hypha-like structures and are saprophytic. Examples: slime moulds and water moulds.

blocks.title: Protists that cause disease
blocks.text: Certain protists are parasitic. Plasmodium causes malaria, Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery, and Trypanosoma causes sleeping sickness.

Fungi are eukaryotic, heterotrophic organisms that are unicellular or multicellular. Their cells are covered by a cell wall made of chitin, a polysaccharide. Fungi get their nutrients in a unique way: they do not ingest food like animals and some protists do. Instead they absorb food from their surroundings. Examples are mushrooms, rusts, smuts and moulds.

items: Zygomycota are fungi whose hyphae lack septa (cross walls). Example: Rhizopus, the bread mould, which grows on moist bread and fruit.
Ascomycota is the largest group of fungi. They have septate hyphae. Examples: common moulds, morels, truffles, cup fungi, Neurospora and yeasts.
Basidiomycota also have septate hyphae. Examples: mushrooms, toadstools, puffballs, jelly fungi, bracket or shelf fungi, rusts and smuts.

blocks.title: Fungi in daily life
blocks.text: Some fungi are used to make bread, cheese and beer. Others have medicinal properties: penicillin, an antibiotic, is derived from the fungus Penicillium. There are about 100,000 known species of fungi. Most ascomycetes are found in lichens, and some are found in mycorrhizae (partnerships with plant roots).

Kingdom Plantae includes plants: eukaryotic, multicellular organisms with cell walls made of cellulose. They are autotrophic and make their food by photosynthesis. All plants develop from embryos. Examples are mosses, ferns, conifers and flowering plants.

items: Non-vascular plants, or bryophytes, lack conducting tissues (xylem and phloem). Examples: liverworts, hornworts and mosses.
Vascular plants have conducting tissues. They are of two types: seedless plants, such as ferns, and seed plants, such as conifers (pine, Cedrus, Ginkgo) and flowering plants (capsicum, mustard).

blocks.alt: A branching chart. Kingdom Plantae splits into non-vascular plants (bryophytes: moss, liverwort, hornwort) and vascular plants. Vascular plants split into seedless plants (ferns) and seed plants (conifers and flowering plants).
blocks.caption: The major groups of kingdom Plantae (original chart after Figure 1.8).
blocks.long_description: Plants are first divided by whether they have conducting tissue. Vascular plants are then divided by whether they make seeds. Seed plants include conifers such as pine and Cedrus and flowering plants such as capsicum and mustard.

blocks.text: This kingdom of eukaryotes includes animals, which are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic. They develop from embryos. They ingest food and digest it inside their bodies. The classification of kingdom Animalia into phyla is the subject of the next topic.
The kingdoms of the three domains compared

The textbook summarises the kingdoms in one table. Bacteria and Archaea are both shown under the old kingdom name Monera, because the five-kingdom system placed every prokaryote there. Read each column as a profile of one kingdom.

blocks.caption: Distinguishing characteristics of the kingdoms of the three domains
rows: Photosynthetic or heterotroph, or a combination

items: Protista: unicellular, colonial, filamentous or simply multicellular eukaryotes; animal-like protozoa, plant-like algae and fungi-like slime and water moulds.
Fungi: chitin walls; absorb food rather than ingest it; Zygomycota (no septa), Ascomycota and Basidiomycota (septate hyphae).
Plantae: cellulose walls, photosynthetic, develop from embryos; non-vascular bryophytes and vascular plants (seedless and seed plants).
Animalia: multicellular, heterotrophic, develop from embryos, ingest and digest food internally.
Only animals lack a cell wall; only fungi have chitin walls; only plants have cellulose walls with photosynthetic autotrophy in every member.

blocks.prompt: A multicellular eukaryote absorbs food from its surroundings and has cell walls of chitin. Which kingdom is it in, and which other kingdom is ruled out by the cell wall alone?
blocks.explanation: It is a fungus. A chitin wall rules out Plantae, whose walls are cellulose, and Animalia, which have no cell wall at all.
